neighbours.label: The preposition after a participle that opens a fixed complement ('flown at half-staff', 'tightened to a torque', 'armed to the teeth'), vs the same preposition in a free locative phrase
fire: All public buildings will fly their flags at half-staff until Friday.
After the bombing, flags across the city were lowered to half-mast.
The wheel nuts must be tightened to 120 newton metres.
The rebels arrived armed to the teeth with rifles and grenades.
The governor ordered that flags be flown at half-staff on Monday.
Each bolt is torqued to the value printed in the manual.
Flags at the embassy flew at half-staff for three days.
The cylinder head screws were tightened to the recommended torque.
quiet: All public buildings will fly their flags at the new plaza on Friday.
After the bombing, crowds across the city gathered in the square.
The wheel nuts are stored in a box at the garage.
The rebels arrived at the village with rifles and grenades.
The governor ordered that flags be sold at the fair on Monday.
Each bolt is kept in the drawer printed in the manual.
Flags at the embassy hung in the hall for three days.
The cylinder head screws were found in the toolbox.

predictions: 'at half-staff', 'tightened to', 'armed to the teeth' 0.3-0.9; locative 'at the corner', 'met at the cafe' under 0.12.
notes: Card: ' at' x8 (fired at, flown at half-staff x2), ' to' x11 (tightened to a torque, armed to the teeth), ' in' x6. Probe: 'flown at half-staff' 0.873, 'tightened to the specified torque' 0.377, 'fired at the convoy' 0.199, 'fit to data' 0.109, 'found in the retina' 0.063; 'house at the corner' 0.012, 'met at the cafe' 0.005.
